newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate falls on foreign bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate falls on foreign bank lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to as low as 6.0 percent on Friday on lending by foreign banks which now find themselves flush with ringgit, dealers said.
"Foreign banks were giving from 8.0 percent all the way down to 6.0 percent. They are still long," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

Foreign banks accumulated large ringgit positions last month when the Malaysian currency came under attack from speculators who were driving down the ringgit in the wake of a financial crisis in Thailand.
The overnight traded between 6.5 and 9.0 percent on Thursday.
Dealers said the rate also fell as fears the Malaysian central bank would impose capital controls like those in Thailand faded.
Interbank rates were firm on Thursday on the capital controls talk which started when the central bank called for a meeting on Friday with chief executive officers of some banks.
But banking sources said the meeting was to discuss routine foreign exchange activities.
Dealers said persistent rumours of a cut in the statutory reserve requirement (SRR) due to the current tight liquidity situation also pressured the overnight rate.
Dealers, however, maintained that it was unlikely Bank Negara would take any action.
A cut in the SRR, currently at 13.5 percent, would send a wrong signal to the market, as monetary and consumption growth were still high, they said.
Dealers said the maturity of Bank Negara deposits totalling 1.5 billion ringgit over the next week would provide some liquidity in the market and could push rates lower.
The amount was raised as part of Bank Negara's open market operations. The central bank regularly intervenes in the money market to keep liquidity under check and set interest rates.
Earlier, one-, two- and three-week money were at 8.00/20 percent against 7.5/8.0 percent on Thursday, dealers said.
One-month money was at 8.20/30 percent from 7.9/8.1, and three-month at 8.00/10 percent against 7.9/8.1.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was unchanged at 92.06, or an implied yield of 7.94 percent.
The September contract was up four points at 92.45, or 7.55 percent, and December was up three at 92.54, or 7.46 percent.
